findings.claim: G1 and the Intent say any local folder reaches OpenViking through the bucket, but ov-sync-consumer skips every key under a prefix not in its prefix map (mapping.go Resolve; the map in localstack deployments/applications/services.tf lists only JasperHG90/localstack/ and JasperHG90/loop-engineering-harness/). A laptop also has no write credential: the ov-sync bucket has writers = [] and CI writes only through per-repo ci-<role> STS roles minted from Vault. So ovsq can pass every eval row and still put nothing in OpenViking. The plan must name these localstack changes (a prefixes entry per prefix, an identity or role a laptop can use) as an out-of-repo dependency the operator accepts, or narrow G1/P1 to what this repo can deliver.

The plan keeps the action's manifest format 'so CI and a laptop can share a prefix', but the action deletes every manifest entry its git ls-files does not list, with no opt-out (sync.py main, deletes = [p for p in old if p not in new]). A laptop's uploads under a CI repo's prefix are deleted on the next CI run, and with --delete a laptop run deletes CI's files. The same clash hits two local folders that share one <prefix>/_state/manifest.json through different `subdir` values. The plan also never says whether manifest paths include `subdir`, which decides the keys that deletes compute. Decide one owner per manifest: either refuse to share a prefix, or give each source (or subdir) its own manifest key, and say how subdir appears in keys and manifest paths.

O4 says `fixes: P1`, but O4 only wires the Go gates and writes the README. It does not change how a local folder's documents reach OpenViking. plan.split reads this fact, so O4 should fix no problem, or the problem list should name the one it does fix.
The localstack prefix-map entry and the laptop write credential are now named as outside this ticket and documented in the README. G1 and P1 are narrowed to delivery into the bucket.

Each source owns <prefix>/_state/ovsq-<source>.json and never touches manifest.json. Manifest paths include subdir, so a delete targets exactly <prefix>/<path>. The action only deletes paths in its own manifest, so CI no longer removes ovsq's files unless both write the same key, which the plan names as operator error.
O4 now fixes the new P4 (no Go gates), which it does fix.

When FOLDER is a symlink to a directory, scan.Select walks nothing (filepath.WalkDir Lstats the root and does not descend), so every manifest entry becomes a delete; `ovsq run LINK --delete` removes the whole prefix and exits 0. Config loads through the link, so nothing warns.
The r4 test checks Engine.Run's Result.Failed, not the CLI exit code, so the row's "the run exits 0" clause is only covered indirectly through main.go's `res.Failed > 0` branch.
The reference page and usage text say exit 2 means a config error, but a missing include_folders entry and a failed git ls-files (both config problems) come back from Prepare and exit 1.

On Ctrl-C the final manifest write uses the cancelled context, so it always fails and the last partial batch's uploads lose their manifest entries (they re-upload next run). Writing the final manifest with context.WithoutCancel(ctx) would keep that progress.
